tagAlarms.intro: Define the conditions that trigger an alarm. You can add several independent rules (e.g. “High” at 80 + “Critical high” at 95).
tagAlarms.empty_title: No alarms set up for this tag.
tagAlarms.empty_hint: Click “New alarm” to create the first rule.
tagAlarms.delay_help_comm_loss: Triggers after {{seconds}}s without valid readings. 0 = use 60s.
tagAlarms.delay_help_frozen: Triggers after {{seconds}}s without the value changing. 0 = use 60s.
tagAlarms.delay_help: The condition must hold for {{seconds}}s before it triggers (debounce).
tagAlarms.deadband_help_frozen: The value counts as frozen while it moves by less than {{value}}.
tagAlarms.deadband_help: To clear, the value must move at least {{value}} back past the threshold.
tagAlarms.message_placeholder: Shown in active alarms and in notifications
tagAlarms.message_help: Generated from the condition; you can customise it (e.g. “Pump P1 tripped”).

lorawan.title: LoRaWAN devices — {{gateway}}
lorawan.subtitle: Devices appear automatically when they send their first uplink. Pick the fields to import as OpenEdge tags.
lorawan.empty_desc: The driver registers each device as soon as it sends its first uplink to the network server.
lorawan.downlink_note: The downlink is queued on the network server (TTN/ChirpStack) and delivered to the device on its next uplink.

inventoryPage.title: Device inventory
inventoryPage.subtitle: Everything installed: address, protocol, status and last contact. This is the document to hand to a customer or an inspector.
inventoryPage.search_placeholder: Search by name, site, address, protocol…

udtTypesPage.title: Types (UDT)
udtTypesPage.subtitle: A type describes a piece of equipment once. Every instance is generated from it and stays linked: change the type and all instances follow.
udtTypesPage.empty: No types defined. Create one when you have several pieces of the same equipment — ten pumps, twenty valves — instead of creating their tags by hand one by one.
udtTypesPage.create_desc: Name the type; you define its members right after.
udtTypesPage.name_help: Letters, digits, dash and underscore. The name goes into the alias of the generated tags, and so into an MQTT topic.
udtTypesPage.delete_has_instances_one: This type has {{count}} instance. The delete will be refused: delete the instance first — it is real equipment.
udtTypesPage.delete_has_instances_other: This type has {{count}} instances. The delete will be refused: delete the instances first — they are real equipment.
udtTypesPage.delete_no_instances: The type has no instances, so no tags are generated or deleted.

udtInstancesPage.title: Instances
udtInstancesPage.subtitle: An instance is a type applied to a gateway at a base address. Its tags are generated right away: base address + member suffix.
udtInstancesPage.empty_no_types: Define a type first, then you can create instances of it.
udtInstancesPage.empty: No instances. Create one to generate the tags of a piece of equipment.
udtInstancesPage.create_desc: Tags are generated right away. Check the first one on the PLC before creating more: a wrong base address multiplies silently.
udtInstancesPage.name_help_suffix: That way an alarm tells you which machine it comes from.
udtInstancesPage.base_address_help: Member suffixes are appended to it:
udtInstancesPage.delete_desc_one: {{count}} tag will be deleted, along with all its recorded history. It can only be recovered from a backup.
udtInstancesPage.delete_desc_other: {{count}} tags will be deleted, along with all their recorded history. They can only be recovered from a backup.

udtEditor.no_instances: No instances: changes don't affect anything yet.
udtEditor.instances_one: {{count}} instance. Every change here reaches it.
udtEditor.instances_other: {{count}} instances. Every change here reaches all of them.
udtEditor.suffix_help: The suffix is appended to the instance's base address:
udtEditor.loss_removing: You are removing from the type:
udtEditor.loss_tags_one: tag will be deleted from the instances of this type.
udtEditor.loss_tags_other: tags will be deleted from the instances of this type.
udtEditor.loss_rows_one: recorded history row will be lost with them.
udtEditor.loss_rows_other: recorded history rows will be lost with them.
udtEditor.loss_hint: It can only be recovered from a backup. If you just want to stop recording that value, turn off historize on the member instead of removing it.

tagsPage.title: Tags
tagsPage.subtitle: Manage the data points read from the PLCs, their history and alarms.
tagsPage.create_desc: Add a new tag to the gateway.
tagsPage.code_modbus_help: Generated by the builder above, or type it by hand
tagsPage.code_mqtt_help: Enter the exact MQTT topic the PLC publishes to.
tagsPage.json_path_help: For JSON payloads: extracts the field at this path (dot notation). Leave empty if the payload is the value itself.
tagsPage.scaling_enabled_help: Converts the raw value (e.g. 4–20 mA) to engineering units before it is stored and sent.
tagsPage.clamp: Clamp output to the EU range
tagsPage.clamp_help: Out-of-range values are clamped to EU min / EU max
tagsPage.scaling_off: Enable EU scaling to set up the raw → engineering-unit mapping.
tagsPage.live_disconnected: Live feed disconnected — values below may be stale
tagsPage.browse_desc: Navigate the OPC UA address space. Click an Object node to open it, or “Add as tag” on a Variable node to create a tag.
tagsPage.write_desc: Send a value to the PLC. This action is logged.
